--- One tmux invocation for many directories.
--- Use this + is_running_in() when checking N directories in a loop;
--- is_running_for_directory() spawns a tmux process per call.
--- @return table<string, boolean> set of running tmux session names
function M.running_set()
	local set = {}
	for _, name in ipairs(list_oc_sessions()) do
		set[name] = true
	end
	return set
end

--- Pure membership lookup -- no subprocess.
--- @param set table<string, boolean> result of M.running_set()
--- @param cwd string project directory
--- @return boolean
function M.is_running_in(set, cwd)
	if not set or not cwd or cwd == "" then
		return false
	end
	return set[session_name(cwd)] == true
end

				return "STALLED"
			end
			return "RUNNING"
		end
		return "IDLE"
	end

reason: Fix the 5-10s picker lag in ONE place, with no viewer.lua edit. is_running_for_directory() currently spawns a tmux process per call, and viewer.lua's picker calls it once per session row (654). Wrapping it in a 2-second cache that reuses the already-applied M.running_set()/M.is_running_in() collapses the whole burst into a single tmux call. This replaces the approach of editing viewer.lua lines 700-740, which the console refused as an unbalanced edit. New group slug because ae-picker-tmux-batch already has an applied sessions.lua entry that the console would treat as an older revision and skip.

-- The session picker checks every row in one burst; without a short cache that
-- is one tmux spawn per session (654 sessions => multi-second open). The set
-- enumerates every live tmux session, so a directory absent from it is simply
-- not running — no extra spawn needed to decide.
local running_cache, running_cache_at = nil, 0
local RUNNING_CACHE_TTL = 2

--- Cached for RUNNING_CACHE_TTL seconds. A burst of checks costs one tmux
--- call (M.running_set()) instead of one per directory.
function M.is_running_for_directory(cwd)
	if not cwd or cwd == "" then
		return false
	end
	local now = os.time()
	if not running_cache or now - running_cache_at >= RUNNING_CACHE_TTL then
		running_cache = M.running_set()
		running_cache_at = now
	end
	return M.is_running_in(running_cache, cwd)
end

reason: The gate counts delimiters across the whole resulting file and demands absolute zero, so every edit to a file whose string literals contain a delimiter is refused forever regardless of the fragment. viewer.lua has ~+20 depth from Lua pattern strings and can never be edited. This keeps the guard (still refuses a genuine unbalancing) but compares before vs after, and reports the range, line counts, before/after depths and the offending replacement lines. Byte comparisons instead of "{" / "(" literals keep this block itself at delta zero.
content:
-- Delimiter balance guard (doc 21 follow-up): an edit_range that leaves the
	-- FILE less balanced than it found it can kill a plugin at load -- not
	-- hypothetical, it happened. The count is deliberately naive: strings and
	-- comments are included. So compare the resulting file against the original
	-- and refuse only a CHANGE in balance. Requiring absolute zero refuses every
	-- edit to a file that carries delimiter characters inside string literals.
	if op == "edit_range" then
		local ext = vim.fn.fnamemodify(path, ":e"):lower()
		if ext == "ts" or ext == "tsx" or ext == "js" or ext == "lua" then
			local function net_delims(text)
				local d = 0
				for ch in text:gmatch("[%{%(}%)]") do
					local b = ch:byte()
					if b == 123 or b == 40 then
						d = d + 1
					else
						d = d - 1
					end
				end
				return d
			end
			local before = exists and net_delims(table.concat(vim.fn.readfile(path), "\n")) or 0
			local after = net_delims(content)
			local delta = after - before
			if delta ~= 0 then
				local off, n = {}, 0
				for i, l in ipairs(vim.split(content, "\n", { plain = true })) do
					n = i
					local d = 0
					for ch in l:gmatch("[%{%(}%)]") do
						local b = ch:byte()
						if b == 123 or b == 40 then
							d = d + 1
						else
							d = d - 1
						end
					end
					if d ~= 0 and #off < 6 then
						off[#off + 1] = string.format("    line %d: %+d  %s", i, d, l:sub(1, 72))
					end
				end
				local detail = #off > 0 and table.concat(off, "\n")
					or "    no single line is off -- a string literal with a delimiter is the likely cause"
				local choice = vim.fn.confirm(
					string.format(
						"⚠️ Unbalanced edit: this CHANGES delimiter balance by %+d.\n  %s\n  range: %s-%s   replacement lines: %d\n  file before: %+d   after: %+d\n  Offending replacement lines:\n%s\n\nAn unbalanced apply can kill the plugin at load. Apply anyway?",
						delta,
						path,
						tostring(proposal.start_line),
						tostring(proposal.end_line),
						n,
						before,
						after,
						detail
					),
					"&No\n&Yes",
					1
				)
				if choice ~= 2 then
					vim.notify(
						string.format(
							"❌ Refused: unbalanced edit -- balance would change by %+d on %s (range %s-%s). Full detail in :messages.",
							delta,
							path,
							tostring(proposal.start_line),
							tostring(proposal.end_line)
						),
						vim.log.levels.WARN
					)
					return false
				end
			end
		end
	end

reason: Implements "main session, or closest to the workspace root" instead of most-recent. Replaces viewer.lua:484-596 in one balanced range: (1) workspace root is the tmux pane dir with nvim cwd as fallback; (2) get_last_session no longer early-returns, so a stale pin cannot mask newer sessions; (3) all lookups become candidates deduped by sid, then sorted main-first, then by path segments shared with the root, with time_updated only as a tiebreak. Per-path CANDIDATE logs collapse into one RANK list naming tier, main flag and shared-segment count, which is the decision point worth logging. Region 484-596 nets to delimiter depth 0 and this replacement does too, so the gate sees delta 0. sessions.lua is already applied, so runtime.main_session() exists.
content:
-- Workspace root: the tmux pane dir wins over nvim's cwd, so switching panes
	-- changes what opens. One nvim per tmux session makes the pane the faithful
	-- signal.
	local runtime = require("opencode-ext.sessions")
	local root = vim.fn.isdirectory(tmux_dir) == 1 and tmux_dir or cwd
	local main_name, main_dir, main_sid = runtime.main_session()

	-- Gather every candidate. The pin is a candidate like any other now: it used
	-- to early-return, and that is what made this "never get the latest".
	local candidates = {}
	local seen = {}

	local function add(s, tier)
		if not s or not s.sid or s.sid == vim.NIL or seen[s.sid] then
			return
		end
		seen[s.sid] = true
		s.tier = tier
		table.insert(candidates, s)
	end

	local last_sid = get_last_session(root)
	if last_sid then
		add(db.fetch_session(last_sid), "pinned")
	end
	add(db.fetch_by_worktree(root), "exact")
	add(db.fetch_all(root), "parent")
	add(db.fetch_global_by_directory(root), "global")

	if #candidates == 0 then
		vim.notify("[ae] NO CANDIDATES for root=" .. root, vim.log.levels.WARN)
		vim.notify("opencode: no session under " .. root, vim.log.levels.WARN)
		return
	end

	-- Rank: main session first, then whichever candidate sits closest to the
	-- workspace root, then most recent. Recency alone is what dragged in
	-- unrelated sessions, so it is only a tiebreak now.
	local function shared_prefix_segments(p)
		local rp = vim.split(root, "/", { plain = true })
		local pp = vim.split(p or "", "/", { plain = true })
		local n = 0
		while n < #rp and n < #pp and rp[n + 1] == pp[n + 1] do
			n = n + 1
		end
		return n
	end

	local function project_of(s)
		return db.fetch_session_project(s.sid) or (s.project or "")
	end

	table.sort(candidates, function(a, b)
		local am = (main_sid and a.sid == main_sid) and 1 or 0
		local bm = (main_sid and b.sid == main_sid) and 1 or 0
		if am ~= bm then
			return am > bm
		end
		local ap = shared_prefix_segments(project_of(a))
		local bp = shared_prefix_segments(project_of(b))
		if ap ~= bp then
			return ap > bp
		end
		return (a.time_updated or 0) > (b.time_updated or 0)
	end)

	for i, c in ipairs(candidates) do
		vim.notify(
			"[ae] RANK "
				.. i
				.. " tier="
				.. tostring(c.tier)
				.. " main="
				.. (main_sid and c.sid == main_sid and "yes" or "no")
				.. " shared="
				.. shared_prefix_segments(project_of(c))
				.. " sid="
				.. tostring(c.sid),
			vim.log.levels.INFO
		)
	end

	local chosen = candidates[1]
